reason: The trigger is real and fresh: Blitzy announced a $200M Series B led by Northzone at a $1.4B valuation on 5 May 2026 (BusinessWire; Boston Globe; Crunchbase News), with PSG, Battery Ventures, Jump Capital, Morgan Creek Digital and Defiant joining and Flybridge, Link Ventures, NFX, Picus Capital and Venture Guides returning. The founders are verified: Brian Elliott (CEO; former Army Ranger, West Point, Harvard MBA) and Sid Pardeshi (CTO; seven years at Nvidia, 25+ patents), Kendall Square, Cambridge MA, founded 2023, ~80 staff, ~$206M raised in total (PitchBook via the Globe). Re-scored honestly against the 5-pillar model it does not clear the MD threshold of 70: capacity 13/20 (a $1.4B company with ~$206M raised in total and 80 people is a $1-2M-a-year partner at most), brand fit 11/20 (an enterprise developer tool with no marketing leadership listed and no consumer or capital-markets audience that a Formula 1 platform reaches), urgency 12/20 (no listing, no product launch tied to a race calendar), timing 16/20, ops fit 13/20 (a plausible but generic 'modernise the team's in-house software' workstream; Cognition at Aston Martin, Claude at Williams and Gemini at McLaren already own the AI-coding lane on the grid with an order of magnitude more capital, so Blitzy would enter as a follower). Total 65/100. The thin row's 78 was inflated by the unicorn headline. Not built; re-surface on a Series C above $5B, a named CMO or CRO hire, or a Fortune 500 customer announcement with a racing tie. No motorsport tie found for either founder after checking.
